# google_network_management_network_monitoring_provider

A Network Monitoring Provider resource that allows third-party network monitoring
solutions to integrate with Google Cloud Network Management. A provider acts as
the parent resource for MonitoringPoints, NetworkPaths, and WebPaths.


To get more information about NetworkMonitoringProvider, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/network-intelligence-center/docs/reference/rest)
* How-to Guides
    * [Network Monitoring overview](https://cloud.google.com/network-intelligence-center/docs/network-monitoring/overview)

## Example Usage - Network Management Network Monitoring Provider Basic


```hcl
resource "google_network_management_network_monitoring_provider" "provider" {
  network_monitoring_provider_id = "my-provider"
  location                       = "global"
  provider_type                  = "EXTERNAL"
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `provider_type` -
  (Required)
  The type of the Network Monitoring Provider.
  Currently only `EXTERNAL` is supported.

* `location` -
  (Required)
  The location of the Network Monitoring Provider. Currently only `global` is supported.

* `network_monitoring_provider_id` -
  (Required)
  The ID to use for the Network Monitoring Provider. This will become the last
  component of the provider's resource name.


* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
* `force_destroy` - (Optional) If set to true, all nested resources (MonitoringPoints, NetworkPaths, WebPaths)
belonging to this provider will also be deleted on provider deletion.



## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/networkMonitoringProviders/{{network_monitoring_provider_id}}`

* `name` -
  The full resource name of the Network Monitoring Provider, in the format
  `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/networkMonitoringProviders/{id}`.

* `provider_uri` -
  Link to the provider's UI.

* `create_time` -
  The time the Network Monitoring Provider was created.

* `update_time` -
  The time the Network Monitoring Provider was last updated.

* `state` -
  The current state of the Network Monitoring Provider.

* `errors` -
  The list of error messages detected for the Network Monitoring Provider.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


NetworkMonitoringProvider can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/networkMonitoringProviders/{{network_monitoring_provider_id}}`
* `{{project}}/{{location}}/{{network_monitoring_provider_id}}`
* `{{location}}/{{network_monitoring_provider_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import NetworkMonitoringProvider using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    location = "<-required value->"
    networkMonitoringProviderId = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_network_management_network_monitoring_provider.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import NetworkMonitoringProvider using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/networkMonitoringProviders/{{network_monitoring_provider_id}}"
  to = google_network_management_network_monitoring_provider.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), NetworkMonitoringProvider can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_network_management_network_monitoring_provider.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/networkMonitoringProviders/{{network_monitoring_provider_id}}
$ terraform import google_network_management_network_monitoring_provider.default {{project}}/{{location}}/{{network_monitoring_provider_id}}
$ terraform import google_network_management_network_monitoring_provider.default {{location}}/{{network_monitoring_provider_id}}
```
